faqs.question: Why would FBR reverse a declared value?
faqs.answer: Usually because the declared value does not match supporting records — invoices, POS data, or import documents. Gaps between what was declared and what the data shows invite adjustment.

faqs.question: How does accurate POS invoicing help?
faqs.answer: When every sale is reported to FBR IRIS in real time, your declared sales values are backed by verifiable records, leaving little room for a reversal. Consistent data is the best defence.

faqs.question: What should I do if I receive a reversal notice?
faqs.answer: Gather the supporting records, respond within the stated window, and correct any genuine errors. Accurate, reconciled POS and tax records make the response far simpler.

faqs.question: What is the FBR POS invoicing system?

faqs.answer: Yes — it looks like a normal receipt but carries a QR code. Scanning it lets anyone confirm on the FBR portal that the sale was genuinely reported, which is the proof of compliance.

faqs.question: What makes an invoice 'valid' under this system?
faqs.answer: That it was accepted by IRIS and the QR encodes the reference IRIS returned. A locally printed receipt with no matching IRIS record is not a valid FBR invoice, even if it looks the part.

faqs.question: Is the whole thing automatic?
faqs.answer: Once configured, yes. The POS submits, IRIS validates and returns a reference, the POS prints the QR — all in the moment of sale, with no manual steps for staff.

title: FBR POS System Issues: Common Errors and How to Fix Them
metaDescription: FBR POS system issues like token expiry, offline sync failures, and QR errors — what causes them and the practical fixes that keep your IRIS integration compliant.

faqs.question: Why does my FBR POS keep showing token expiry errors?
faqs.answer: FBR IRIS authentication tokens expire roughly every 60 minutes. If your POS caches the first token and never refreshes it, every sale after the first hour silently fails. The fix is proactive refresh — request a new token about five minutes before expiry rather than waiting for a rejection.

faqs.question: What happens to sales made while the internet is down?
faqs.answer: A correctly built POS queues those invoices locally and submits them to FBR IRIS when the connection returns, stamped with the original sale time. If your system batches them with the reconnection time instead, FBR's monitoring flags the timestamp mismatch as a discrepancy.

faqs.question: Why is the QR code on my invoice not validating on the FBR portal?
faqs.answer: Usually because the invoice was never accepted by IRIS (a failed submission still prints a receipt locally) or the QR encodes the wrong invoice reference number. Verify the invoice actually appears in your IRIS dashboard before trusting the printed QR.

faqs.question: Can FBR fine me for POS integration errors I did not notice?
faqs.answer: Yes. Non-compliance penalties start around PKR 10,000 and can reach PKR 1,000,000 for repeated violations, plus possible STRN suspension. Silent submission failures are the most dangerous because the business believes it is compliant while invoices never reach FBR.

faqs.question: How often should I reconcile my POS with the IRIS dashboard?
faqs.answer: At least monthly, and ideally weekly. Compare the invoice count your POS recorded against the count IRIS shows. Any gap points to rejected or unsynced invoices you can fix before they become an audit problem.

title: FBR IRIS Portal: How to Register Your POS in Pakistan
metaDescription: A step-by-step guide to registering your POS on the FBR IRIS portal in Pakistan — what you need, how to get API credentials, and the errors that trip people up.

faqs.question: What do I need before registering on the IRIS portal?
faqs.answer: An active STRN, your NTN, business details, and the number of POS terminals you plan to register. Have your login for iris.fbr.gov.pk ready; without an active STRN you cannot complete POS registration.

faqs.question: Where do I get the API credentials for my POS?
faqs.answer: After registering your terminals on the IRIS POS section, FBR issues API credentials (a token/key) that your POS software uses to submit invoices. Your POS vendor configures these so sales report automatically.

faqs.question: How many terminals should I register?
faqs.answer: Register one per active point of sale. If you add a counter or a new branch later, register its terminal before it starts trading — selling on an unregistered terminal is non-compliant.

faqs.question: What is the most common registration mistake?
faqs.answer: Starting to bill before the terminal is fully registered and the API credentials are live in the POS. The receipts print, but nothing reaches FBR until registration is complete.

faqs.answer: Manual compilation from spreadsheets is where mistakes creep in. When the return draws directly from reported POS data, the sales figures match what FBR already has, so there are no discrepancies to explain later.

faqs.question: What happens if some invoices never reached FBR?
faqs.answer: Then your return understates sales and the gap can surface in an audit. This is why a monthly reconciliation between your POS and the IRIS dashboard matters before you file.

faqs.question: Do takeaway and delivery orders need FBR invoices too?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every taxable sale — dine-in, takeaway, or delivery — must generate an FBR-reported, QR-coded invoice. Delivery orders routed through aggregators still need a compliant invoice from your own POS.

faqs.question: How is service charge handled on an FBR invoice?
faqs.answer: Service charge is part of the taxable value unless your tax advisor confirms otherwise, so it must appear on the invoice and be included in what is reported to IRIS. Misclassifying it is a common cause of reconciliation gaps.

faqs.question: Can my restaurant POS keep billing if the internet drops mid-service?
faqs.answer: A compliant POS queues orders locally during an outage and submits them to FBR IRIS with their original timestamps once the connection returns, so a Friday-night rush is never blocked by connectivity.

faqs.question: What happens if a waiter voids an order after the invoice is generated?
faqs.answer: Voids and modifications must be recorded and reported, not just deleted locally. An invoice that exists in IRIS but was cancelled only on the POS creates a discrepancy FBR can flag.

title: How to Generate FBR QR Invoices in Pakistan (and Why They Fail)
metaDescription: A clear guide to generating valid FBR QR invoices in Pakistan — what the QR encodes, the step-by-step process, and the reasons QR codes fail to verify.

faqs.question: What information does an FBR QR code actually contain?
faqs.answer: It encodes the invoice reference issued by FBR IRIS so anyone can verify, on the FBR portal, that the sale was genuinely reported. A QR that points to nothing in IRIS is just a picture — it proves no compliance.

faqs.question: Why does my QR code fail to validate on the FBR portal?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the invoice was never accepted by IRIS — a failed submission still prints a receipt locally — or the QR encodes the wrong reference. Confirm the invoice exists in your IRIS dashboard before trusting the QR.

faqs.question: Do I need a special printer to produce QR invoices?
faqs.answer: No. Any thermal or standard printer works, and you can even send the QR invoice over WhatsApp or SMS. The QR is data, not special hardware; what matters is that the underlying invoice reached FBR.

faqs.question: Can I generate FBR QR invoices without specialised POS hardware?
faqs.answer: Yes — a compliant POS app on a phone, tablet, or laptop can generate valid FBR QR invoices. The requirement is the IRIS integration, not expensive terminals.

faqs.answer: No. FBR compliance and DRAP requirements are separate. A good pharmacy POS helps with both — reporting sales to FBR IRIS while also tracking batches and expiry for DRAP — but neither obligation removes the other.

faqs.question: How does batch and expiry tracking interact with FBR invoicing?
faqs.answer: Batch and expiry tracking is for stock and DRAP, while the FBR invoice reports the sale and tax. They live in the same POS but serve different rules; the invoice still has to reach IRIS regardless of how stock is tracked.

faqs.question: Are all medicines taxed the same way on an FBR invoice?
faqs.answer: No — many medicines fall under specific or exempt categories. Mapping each product to the correct tax treatment is essential; applying a standard rate to exempt items over-charges patients and produces wrong FBR submissions.

faqs.question: What is the penalty risk for a small pharmacy?
faqs.answer: Even small pharmacies that are Tier-1 retailers face penalties starting around PKR 10,000 and rising for repeat non-compliance, plus possible STRN suspension. Silent submission failures are the usual cause.
